# Exportwalla

> Exportwalla is an export desk for Indian manufacturers. Free tools give the HS code, the best destination countries, the import duty
> an Indian product pays in 66 countries (including India–UK CETA, India–UAE CEPA, India–Australia ECTA and
> ASEAN–India rates), named UK importers, a landed-cost quote and export documents. A human desk then handles IEC,
> RCMC, freight, customs, certificates of origin, LC, e-BRC and refunds, paid per shipment. Data verified 2026-11-02.

Duty figures come from the UK Trade Tariff, USITC HTS and World Bank WITS/TRAINS and link to their source. Market
indicators are derived from UN Comtrade. Trade-agreement facts are researched with a source URL each.

## Reference pages
- [Export by country](http://localhost:8040/export-to): duty, trade deal, certificate of origin and import VAT for 66 countries
- [HS codes and duty](http://localhost:8040/hs-code): 357 export products with UK/US lines and duty by country
- [India's trade agreements](http://localhost:8040/fta): 19 agreements, status, which products pay less, how to claim
- [Where India exports](http://localhost:8040/india-exports): top markets and product chapters as shares
- [How to export from India](http://localhost:8040/guide/how-to-export-from-india): IEC to e-BRC, step by step
- [Export guides](http://localhost:8040/guide): IEC, RCMC, HS codes, certificate of origin, GST LUT, RoDTEP, pricing, Incoterms, LC, ECGC, buyers, shipping; plus product guides
- [Free tools](http://localhost:8040/tools): HS code finder, import duty checker, export price calculator, export readiness check
- [Pricing](http://localhost:8040/pricing): free tools; export desk from ₹12,000 per shipment + GST; [contact](http://localhost:8040/contact)
- [Export kaise kare (Hinglish)](http://localhost:8040/hi/export-kaise-kare)
- [About Exportwalla](http://localhost:8040/about) and [sources and licences](http://localhost:8040/sources)
- [Export to United Kingdom](http://localhost:8040/export-to/united-kingdom)
- [Export to United Arab Emirates](http://localhost:8040/export-to/united-arab-emirates)

## Page URL patterns
- `/export-to/{country}`: one country (e.g. `/export-to/united-kingdom`)
- `/hs-code/{hs6}-{name}`: one product (e.g. `/hs-code/640391-leather-footwear-covering-the-ankle-outer-soles-of-rubber`)
- `/export/{product}/{country}`: one product to one country, with duty, landed cost, documents and buyers
- `/fta/{agreement}`: one trade agreement

Every page is also available as markdown: append `.md` to its URL. The key pages in one file: http://localhost:8040/llms-full.txt

## API (JSON, no key)
- `GET http://localhost:8040/api/public/duty?hs6=640391&country=GBR`: duty for Indian goods vs normal duty, with source
- `GET http://localhost:8040/api/public/country/ARE`: trade deal, origin document, VAT, top products
- `GET http://localhost:8040/api/public/product/090931`: HS line, UK/US lines, ranked markets
- `GET http://localhost:8040/api/public/classify?q=leather+chelsea+boots`: HS code candidates for a product description
- OpenAPI: http://localhost:8040/openapi.json

## MCP
- Streamable HTTP endpoint: `http://localhost:8040/mcp`. Tools: lookup_duty, best_markets, country_rules, classify_product.
- Server card: http://localhost:8040/.well-known/mcp.json

## How to cite
- Quote the page's duty figure with its source link and the "Data verified" date. Rates are guidance, not a customs ruling.

## Contact
- Exportwalla export desk: +91 00000 00000

# About Exportwalla

Exportwalla is an export desk for Indian manufacturers, built for factory owners in clusters like Kanpur, Tiruppur,
Moradabad, Unjha and Panipat who make good products but have not exported, or have exported only through an agent.

## What we do

- **Free, self-serve:** upload a GST certificate, invoice, price list or photo and get your HS code, the best countries for your product,
the duty your buyer pays (with and without a trade deal), named buyers where public records exist, a landed-cost quote and the documents checklist.

- **Paid, per shipment:** a named person at our desk takes you from IEC and RCMC through freight, customs, the certificate of origin,
LC checks, e-BRC and refunds. You stay the exporter of record; licensed signatures stay with you and your CA.

## Where our numbers come from

Every figure comes from a public source and links to it: the UK Trade Tariff and HMRC, the US International Trade Commission, UNCTAD
TRAINS through the World Bank's WITS, UN Comtrade, and official trade-agreement texts. We check 66 countries, 357
export products and 19 trade agreements, and re-verify them against the source before each release. [Sources and licences](http://localhost:8040/sources).

## What we are not

Exportwalla is an independent service. It is not affiliated with the Government of India, DGFT, any export promotion council, HMRC, US CBP or any customs authority. An HS code we suggest is a search result, not a binding customs ruling, and duty rates are for guidance: check the
linked official source before you sign a contract.

## For AI assistants and developers

Every public page has a markdown twin (add .md to the URL). There is a summary for language models at [/llms.txt](http://localhost:8040/llms.txt),
a free JSON API at [/docs](http://localhost:8040/docs), and an MCP server at /mcp with tools to look up duty, rank markets, read country rules and classify products.

## Contact

Call +91 00000 00000, in Hindi or English.

Source page: http://localhost:8040/about

# India's trade agreements: which countries give Indian goods lower duty

India has 18 trade agreements in force with the countries we cover, and one agreed with the EU that is not yet in force.
A deal lowers the duty your buyer pays only when your goods meet its rules of origin and you send the right proof of origin.

**Biggest change in 2026:** the India–UK CETA came into force on 15 July 2026. Of the 2,791 UK commodity codes we
track for Indian export products, 1,792 dropped to 0% for Indian goods and 749 were already 0%. [How to claim it →](http://localhost:8040/fta/india-uk-ceta)

## All agreements

| Agreement | Status | In force since | Countries |
| [GSTP (few goods)](http://localhost:8040/fta/gstp) | In force | 1989-04-19 | Singapore, Bangladesh, Malaysia, South Korea, Vietnam, Indonesia and more |
| [ASEAN–India FTA](http://localhost:8040/fta/asean-india-fta) | In force | 2010-01-01 | Singapore, Malaysia, Vietnam, Indonesia, Thailand, Philippines |
| [APTA](http://localhost:8040/fta/apta) | In force | 1976-06-17 | China, Bangladesh, South Korea, Sri Lanka |
| [India–EFTA TEPA](http://localhost:8040/fta/india-efta-tepa) | In force | 2025-10-01 | Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein  |
| [SAFTA](http://localhost:8040/fta/safta) | In force | 2006-01-01 | Bangladesh, Nepal, Sri Lanka |
| [India–Australia ECTA](http://localhost:8040/fta/india-australia-ecta) | In force | 2022-12-29 | Australia |
| [India–Japan CEPA](http://localhost:8040/fta/india-japan-cepa) | In force | 2011-08-01 | Japan |
| [India–Korea CEPA](http://localhost:8040/fta/india-korea-cepa) | In force | 2010-01-01 | South Korea |
| [India–Malaysia CECA](http://localhost:8040/fta/india-malaysia-ceca) | In force | 2011-07-01 | Malaysia |

| [India–Nepal treaty](http://localhost:8040/fta/india-nepal-treaty) | In force | 2009-10-27 | Nepal |
| [India–Oman CEPA](http://localhost:8040/fta/india-oman-cepa) | In force | 2026-06-01 | Oman |
| [India–Singapore CECA](http://localhost:8040/fta/india-singapore-ceca) | In force | 2005-08-01 | Singapore |

| [India–UAE CEPA](http://localhost:8040/fta/india-uae-cepa) | In force | 2022-05-01 | United Arab Emirates |
| [India–UK CETA](http://localhost:8040/fta/india-uk-ceta) | In force | 2026-07-15 | United Kingdom |
| [India–EU FTA](http://localhost:8040/fta/india-eu-fta) | Agreed, not yet in force | – | Netherlands, Germany, Italy, France, Belgium, Spain and more |

## How to use a trade deal

- **Check your product's rate.** Open your [HS code page](http://localhost:8040/hs-code): each market shows the normal rate and the rate for Indian goods.

- **Check the rule of origin.** Your product must be made in India under the deal's product-specific rule (change of tariff heading, value added, or both).

- **Send the proof of origin.** A certificate of origin from DGFT's Trade Connect (trade.gov.in) or an origin declaration on the invoice, depending on the deal.

- **Keep records.** Customs in the buyer's country can verify origin for years after the shipment.

Data verified 2026-11-02 against the official sources linked on this page.

Source page: http://localhost:8040/fta

# Where India exports: top markets and products (2024)

India's goods exports by destination and by product chapter, as shares of the total, so you can see where Indian
products already sell and where the room is.

**United States is India's largest export market**, taking 18.3% of India's goods exports in 2024.
The top five markets take 39%. Mineral fuels, electrical machinery, machinery, pharmaceuticals and gems lead by product.

## What this means for a small manufacturer

- A big market is not always the best one for your product. Open your [HS code page](http://localhost:8040/hs-code) to see the markets ranked for your product by demand, growth, India's foothold and duty.

- Trade deals change the picture: see [which countries give Indian goods lower duty](http://localhost:8040/fta).

Source: UN Comtrade (India as reporter), shares derived. Shares and changes are calculated by Exportwalla from India's reported exports. See [sources and licences](http://localhost:8040/sources).

Data verified 2026-11-02 against the official sources linked on this page.

Source page: http://localhost:8040/india-exports

# How to export from India: 9 steps from IEC to e-BRC (2026)

**In short:** get an IEC from DGFT, register with your export council, find your HS code, choose a country where
Indian goods pay low duty, find importers who already buy your code, quote FOB, prepare the invoice, packing list and certificate of origin,
ship through your CHA, and claim refunds once the bank issues the e-BRC.

- 
## 1. Get your IEC

The Importer-Exporter Code is a 10-character number from DGFT, linked to your PAN. Apply on the DGFT website with a digital signature; the government fee is ₹500. Without an IEC you cannot file a shipping bill.
- 
## 2. Register with your export promotion council (RCMC)

Each product family has a council: CLE for leather, AEPC for apparel, Spices Board, APEDA, EEPC, EPCH and others. The RCMC unlocks export incentives and buyer-seller meets.
- 
## 3. Find your HS code

Every product has a 6-digit HS code used worldwide and an 8-digit ITC-HS code on Indian shipping bills. The code decides the duty your buyer pays, so get it right first.
- 
## 4. Choose the country

Compare demand, growth, how much the country already buys from India and the duty on Indian goods. Trade agreements like India–UK CETA, India–UAE CEPA and India–Australia ECTA cut duty to zero on many lines.
- 
## 5. Find genuine buyers

Start with importers who already buy your HS code. The UK publishes importer names (HMRC); elsewhere use Indian mission commerce wings, council fairs and verified shipment data. Never ship on open credit to a new buyer.
- 
## 6. Price it: FOB, CIF and landed cost

Quote FOB (your price at the Indian port) and know the buyer's landed cost: freight, insurance, duty and import VAT. A lower duty from a trade deal is a selling point.
- 
## 7. Prepare documents

Proforma and commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin for the trade deal, and product certificates. Preferential certificates are applied for on DGFT Trade Connect.
- 
## 8. Ship and clear Indian customs

File a GST LUT to export without paying IGST, register your AD code at the port, and let your CHA file the shipping bill on ICEGATE.
- 
## 9. Get paid and close out

Use advance payment, a letter of credit or ECGC cover. When the money arrives, the bank issues an e-BRC, which you need for RoDTEP, drawback and GST refunds.

Try steps 3 to 7 on your own product now: [upload an invoice or photo](http://localhost:8040/app). Or read [this guide in Hinglish](http://localhost:8040/hi/export-kaise-kare).
Data verified 2026-11-02 against the official sources linked on this page.

Source page: http://localhost:8040/guide/how-to-export-from-india

# India–UAE CEPA: what it means for Indian exporters

India-UAE Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA).

**In force since 2022-05-01.** Partner: United Arab Emirates. Of the 299 product and country pages we publish for United Arab Emirates, **0** show a lower rate for Indian goods than the normal rate. For 299 more, the deal's lower rate is not yet in our tariff data, so the page shows the normal rate.

Status: **In force**
In force since: **2022-05-01**

Countries: **1**
Lower-duty pages: **0** (of 299 tracked)

## Products where Indian goods pay less

None of the product pages we publish for these countries show a lower rate yet. Check your own HS code in the [workspace](http://localhost:8040/app).

## How to claim the lower duty

Certificate of Origin under India-UAE CEPA (Annex 3E format)
- **Who issues it:** EIC/EIAs (all products), DGFT regional offices, MPEDA, Textiles Committee, Spices Board, APEDA, Coir Board, Central Silk Board, DC Handicrafts, Tobacco Board, and SEZ authorities for their units (DGFT Appendix 2B)
- **How:** Exporter registers on DGFT's electronic CoO platform (coo.dgft.gov.in; DGFT now routes eCoO 2.0 through the Trade Connect ePlatform at trade.gov.in), applies online with a digital signature, picks the agreement and the issuing agency, uploads invoice/packing list and origin-criterion details; agency verifies and issues an e-CoO.
 ([Official rules of origin](https://content.dgft.gov.in/Website/dgftprod/f025f410-65c3-41b8-85c9-78f5059a53f8/Appendix%202B%20(Certificate%20of%20Origin%20%5BPreferential%5D)%20as%20on%2006.02.2023%20(1).pdf))

**Claim the India–UAE CEPA rate on your product**We check your product against the rule of origin and file the certificate with you.Ask about this deal

Step by step: [how to get a certificate of origin](http://localhost:8040/guide/certificate-of-origin) · [getting the HS code right](http://localhost:8040/guide/hs-code-for-export)

India-EU Free Trade Agreement.

**Agreed, not yet in force.** Partners: Netherlands, Germany, Italy, France, Belgium, Spain, Poland, Austria, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Sweden. Of the 398 product and country pages we publish for these countries, **0** show a lower rate for Indian goods than the normal rate.

Status: **Agreed, not yet in force**
In force since: **–**

Countries: **27**
Lower-duty pages: **0** (of 398 tracked)

## Products where Indian goods pay less

None of the product pages we publish for these countries show a lower rate yet. Check your own HS code in the [workspace](http://localhost:8040/app).

## How to claim the lower duty

The agreement is not in force yet, so there is no preference to claim under it. Until it is, Indian goods can use **EU GSP (Standard GSP) - Regulation (EU) 978/2012 to 31 Dec 2026; Regulation (EU) 2026/1395 applies from 1 Jan 2027** on some products, with Statement on origin (REX) for EU GSP; text per Annex 22-07 UCC-IA, on invoice or other commercial document.

**Claim the India–EU FTA rate on your product**We check your product against the rule of origin and file the certificate with you.Ask about this deal

## Questions

**Is the India–EU FTA in force?**

Agreed, not yet in force. It is agreed but cannot be used for duty claims until it enters into force.
**Which countries does the India–EU FTA cover?**

Netherlands, Germany, Italy, France, Belgium, Spain, Poland, Austria, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Sweden.
**How do I claim the lower duty?**

The agreement is not in force yet, so there is no preference to claim under it. Until it is, Indian goods can use EU GSP (Standard GSP) - Regulation (EU) 978/2012 to 31 Dec 2026; Regulation (EU) 2026/1395 applies from 1 Jan 2027 on some products, with Statement on origin (REX) for EU GSP; text per Annex 22-07 UCC-IA, on invoice or other commercial document.
**Does every product get zero duty?**

No. Each tariff line has its own rate and phase-in, and some lines are excluded. Check your HS code's page for the rate on your product. Of the 398 product and country pages we publish for these countries, 0 show a lower rate for Indian goods than the normal rate.

- **How:** Exporter registers on DGFT's electronic CoO platform (coo.dgft.gov.in; DGFT now routes eCoO 2.0 through the Trade Connect ePlatform at trade.gov.in), applies online with a digital signature, picks the agreement and the issuing agency, uploads invoice/packing list and origin-criterion details; agency verifies and issues an e-CoO. GSTP certificate of origin also possible (EIC, MPEDA, Tobacco Board, Textiles Committee) but GSTP concessions cover few lines.
 ([Official rules of origin](https://content.dgft.gov.in/Website/dgftprod/f025f410-65c3-41b8-85c9-78f5059a53f8/Appendix%202B%20(Certificate%20of%20Origin%20%5BPreferential%5D)%20as%20on%2006.02.2023%20(1).pdf))

**Claim the ASEAN–India FTA rate on your product**We check your product against the rule of origin and file the certificate with you.Ask about this deal

## How to claim the lower duty

India-Singapore CECA Certificate of Origin, or AIFTA Form AI
- **Who issues it:** Export Inspection Council (EIC/EIAs) for all goods; MPEDA for marine products; Textiles Committee for textiles and made-ups (DGFT Appendix 2B)
- **How:** Exporter registers on DGFT's electronic CoO platform (coo.dgft.gov.in; DGFT now routes eCoO 2.0 through the Trade Connect ePlatform at trade.gov.in), applies online with a digital signature, picks the agreement and the issuing agency, uploads invoice/packing list and origin-criterion details; agency verifies and issues an e-CoO. GSTP certificate of origin also possible (EIC, MPEDA, Tobacco Board, Textiles Committee) but GSTP concessions cover few lines.
 ([Official rules of origin](https://content.dgft.gov.in/Website/dgftprod/f025f410-65c3-41b8-85c9-78f5059a53f8/Appendix%202B%20(Certificate%20of%20Origin%20%5BPreferential%5D)%20as%20on%2006.02.2023%20(1).pdf))

**Claim the GSTP (few goods) rate on your product**We check your product against the rule of origin and file the certificate with you.Ask about this deal

 ([Official rules of origin](https://content.dgft.gov.in/Website/dgftprod/8d1fc29e-03a5-4a3d-9fda-a602e21e3411/Appendix%202D_new.pdf))

| [T-shirts (cotton, knitted or crocheted)](http://localhost:8040/export/610910-t-shirts-cotton-knitted-or-crocheted/united-kingdom) HS 610910 | United Kingdom | 12% | **0%** |
| [Bed linen and towels (terry towelling or similar terry fabrics)](http://localhost:8040/export/630260-bed-linen-and-towels-terry-towelling-or-similar-terry/united-kingdom) HS 630260 | United Kingdom | 12% | **0%** |
| [Furnishing articles (not knitted or crocheted)](http://localhost:8040/export/630419-furnishing-articles-not-knitted-or-crocheted/united-kingdom) HS 630419 | United Kingdom | 12% | **0%** |
| [Women's suits and dresses (girls', of cotton)](http://localhost:8040/export/620442-women-s-suits-and-dresses-girls-of-cotton/united-kingdom) HS 620442 | United Kingdom | 12% | **0%** |
| [Furnishing articles (cotton, not knitted or crocheted)](http://localhost:8040/export/630492-furnishing-articles-cotton-not-knitted-or-crocheted/united-kingdom) HS 630492 | United Kingdom | 12% | **0%** |

## How to claim the lower duty

CETA origin declaration (Annex 3B template) completed by the Indian exporter/producer, or certificate of origin (Annex 3C) issued by an Indian issuing authority; UK importer may also claim on importer's knowledge
- **Who issues it:** Certificate of origin: authorised agencies notified by the Department of Commerce (DGFT Appendix 2B), applied for electronically on DGFT Trade Connect eCoO; origin declaration: exporter self-declares
- **How:** Apply on DGFT Trade Connect (trade.gov.in) Certificate of Origin service, choosing the agency-issued or self-declaration India-UK CETA route; proof valid 12 months; UK may grant preference without proof for imports up to GBP 1,000 customs value (Chapter 3 low-value derogation). Keep origin records.
 ([Official rules of origin](https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/687e58acae8555bab409a070/uk_india_ceta_chapter_3_rules_of_origin.pdf))

**Claim the India–UK CETA rate on your product**We check your product against the rule of origin and file the certificate with you.Ask about this deal

Step by step: [how to get a certificate of origin](http://localhost:8040/guide/certificate-of-origin) · [getting the HS code right](http://localhost:8040/guide/hs-code-for-export)

# SAFTA: what it means for Indian exporters

Agreement on South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA).

**In force since 2006-01-01.** Partners: Bangladesh, Nepal, Sri Lanka. Of the 17 product and country pages we publish for these countries, **10** show a lower rate for Indian goods than the normal rate. For 7 more, the deal's lower rate is not yet in our tariff data, so the page shows the normal rate.

Status: **In force**
In force since: **2006-01-01**

Countries: **3**
Lower-duty pages: **10** (of 17 tracked)

## How to claim the lower duty

SAFTA Certificate of Origin (or APTA certificate for APTA concessions)
- **Who issues it:** SAFTA: EIC (all goods), MPEDA, Textiles Committee (Appendix 2B); APTA: agencies in Appendix 2D (APEDA, EPCs, FIEO, etc.) plus Textiles Committee
- **How:** Exporter registers on DGFT's electronic CoO platform (coo.dgft.gov.in; DGFT now routes eCoO 2.0 through the Trade Connect ePlatform at trade.gov.in), applies online with a digital signature, picks the agreement and the issuing agency, uploads invoice/packing list and origin-criterion details; agency verifies and issues an e-CoO. GSTP certificate of origin also possible (EIC, MPEDA, Tobacco Board, Textiles Committee) but GSTP concessions cover few lines.
 ([Official rules of origin](https://content.dgft.gov.in/Website/dgftprod/f025f410-65c3-41b8-85c9-78f5059a53f8/Appendix%202B%20(Certificate%20of%20Origin%20%5BPreferential%5D)%20as%20on%2006.02.2023%20(1).pdf))

**Claim the SAFTA rate on your product**We check your product against the rule of origin and file the certificate with you.Ask about this deal

 ([Agreement status, official source](https://rtais.wto.org/UI/PublicShowMemberRTAIDCard.aspx?rtaid=188))

## How to claim the lower duty

MICECA Certificate of Origin (Form MICECA), or AIFTA Form AI
- **Who issues it:** Export Inspection Council (EIC/EIAs) for all goods; MPEDA for marine products; Textiles Committee for textiles and made-ups (DGFT Appendix 2B)
- **How:** Exporter registers on DGFT's electronic CoO platform (coo.dgft.gov.in; DGFT now routes eCoO 2.0 through the Trade Connect ePlatform at trade.gov.in), applies online with a digital signature, picks the agreement and the issuing agency, uploads invoice/packing list and origin-criterion details; agency verifies and issues an e-CoO. GSTP certificate of origin also possible (EIC, MPEDA, Tobacco Board, Textiles Committee) but GSTP concessions cover few lines.
 ([Official rules of origin](https://content.dgft.gov.in/Website/dgftprod/f025f410-65c3-41b8-85c9-78f5059a53f8/Appendix%202B%20(Certificate%20of%20Origin%20%5BPreferential%5D)%20as%20on%2006.02.2023%20(1).pdf))

## How to claim the lower duty

India-MERCOSUR PTA certificate of origin (Annex III Rules of Origin), only for the ~450 tariff lines with concessions
- **Who issues it:** Indian designated issuing agencies via DGFT Trade Connect eCoO (agency-issued)
- **How:** Apply on DGFT Trade Connect Certificate of Origin service under India-MERCOSUR PTA. A First Additional Protocol for electronic certificates of origin was signed in Sep 2026 but is not yet in force, so check whether Brazilian customs still needs the signed paper certificate.
 ([Official rules of origin](https://www.trade.gov.in/pages/certificate-of-origin))

**Claim the India–Mercosur PTA rate on your product**We check your product against the rule of origin and file the certificate with you.Ask about this deal

Step by step: [how to get a certificate of origin](http://localhost:8040/guide/certificate-of-origin) · [getting the HS code right](http://localhost:8040/guide/hs-code-for-export)

## Questions

**Is the India–Mercosur PTA in force?**

In force since 2009-06-01.
**Which countries does the India–Mercosur PTA cover?**

Brazil.
**How do I claim the lower duty?**

India-MERCOSUR PTA certificate of origin (Annex III Rules of Origin), only for the ~450 tariff lines with concessionsWho issues it: Indian designated issuing agencies via DGFT Trade Connect eCoO (agency-issued)How: Apply on DGFT Trade Connect Certificate of Origin service under India-MERCOSUR PTA. A First Additional Protocol for electronic certificates of origin was signed in Sep 2026 but is not yet in force, so check whether Brazilian customs still needs the signed paper certificate. (Official rules of origin)
**Does every product get zero duty?**

No. Each tariff line has its own rate and phase-in, and some lines are excluded. Check your HS code's page for the rate on your product. Of the 27 product and country pages we publish for Brazil, 11 show a lower rate for Indian goods than the normal rate. For 16 more, the deal's lower rate is not yet in our tariff data, so the page shows the normal rate.

## How to claim the lower duty

IKCEPA Certificate of Origin (or APTA certificate)
- **Who issues it:** Export Inspection Council (EIC/EIAs) for all goods; MPEDA for marine products; Textiles Committee for textiles and made-ups (DGFT Appendix 2B)
- **How:** Exporter registers on DGFT's electronic CoO platform (coo.dgft.gov.in; DGFT now routes eCoO 2.0 through the Trade Connect ePlatform at trade.gov.in), applies online with a digital signature, picks the agreement and the issuing agency, uploads invoice/packing list and origin-criterion details; agency verifies and issues an e-CoO. GSTP certificate of origin also possible (EIC, MPEDA, Tobacco Board, Textiles Committee) but GSTP concessions cover few lines.
 ([Official rules of origin](https://content.dgft.gov.in/Website/dgftprod/f025f410-65c3-41b8-85c9-78f5059a53f8/Appendix%202B%20(Certificate%20of%20Origin%20%5BPreferential%5D)%20as%20on%2006.02.2023%20(1).pdf))

**Claim the India–Korea CEPA rate on your product**We check your product against the rule of origin and file the certificate with you.Ask about this deal

Step by step: [how to get a certificate of origin](http://localhost:8040/guide/certificate-of-origin) · [getting the HS code right](http://localhost:8040/guide/hs-code-for-export)

## How to claim the lower duty

IJCEPA Certificate of Origin
- **Who issues it:** Export Inspection Council (EIC/EIAs) for all goods; MPEDA for marine products; Textiles Committee for textiles and made-ups (DGFT Appendix 2B)
- **How:** Exporter registers on DGFT's electronic CoO platform (coo.dgft.gov.in; DGFT now routes eCoO 2.0 through the Trade Connect ePlatform at trade.gov.in), applies online with a digital signature, picks the agreement and the issuing agency, uploads invoice/packing list and origin-criterion details; agency verifies and issues an e-CoO. Operational certification procedures are in the IJCEPA Implementing Procedures.
 ([Official rules of origin](https://content.dgft.gov.in/Website/dgftprod/f025f410-65c3-41b8-85c9-78f5059a53f8/Appendix%202B%20(Certificate%20of%20Origin%20%5BPreferential%5D)%20as%20on%2006.02.2023%20(1).pdf))

from ₹12,000 per shipment + GST
A named person takes your shipment from set-up to payment.

- Certificate of origin filed on DGFT Trade Connect
- Freight quotes, CHA and shipping-bill checks

These are not our fee. We tell you each one before it is incurred: government and export council fees, certificate-of-origin agency fees,
lab tests and certifications, freight and insurance, CHA and port charges, and bank charges.

## Questions

**What does the self-serve plan cost?**

Nothing. The HS code, best countries, duty, buyers, landed-cost quote and documents checklist are free, with no sign-up.
**How is the desk fee charged?**

Per shipment, from ₹12,000 plus GST. We tell you the fee for your shipment in writing before we start. There is no subscription and no commission on your order.
**What is not included in the desk fee?**

Costs paid to others at actuals: government and council fees, certificate-of-origin agency fees, lab tests, freight, insurance, CHA and port charges, and bank charges. We tell you each one before it is incurred.
**Do you take a share of my order or my buyer?**

No. You stay the exporter of record. The buyer, the payment and the refunds are yours; we never take title to your goods.
**Can I use only part of the desk?**

Yes. Many exporters do the self-serve steps themselves and ask the desk only for set-up, documents or the LC check. Call us and we will quote for the part you need.

# How to get an IEC (Importer-Exporter Code) from DGFT

**In short:** An IEC is the 10-character Importer-Exporter Code that DGFT issues against your business PAN. Without it you cannot file a shipping bill or receive export payments through your bank. Apply online at dgft.gov.in, sign with a digital signature or Aadhaar e-sign and pay ₹500. Then confirm or update the IEC online every year between April and June, or it is deactivated.

Government fee: **₹500, one time**
Annual update: **1 April – 30 June, free**
Late annual update: **₹200**
Apply at: **dgft.gov.in**

## Who needs an IEC

Any business that exports or imports goods needs an IEC. Customs will not accept a shipping bill without it, and your bank asks for it before it credits export proceeds. The IEC is tied to the PAN of the business: one PAN, one IEC. For a proprietorship that is the owner's PAN; for a partnership, LLP or company it is the entity's own PAN.
- **Manufacturer exporting in its own name:** needs an IEC.
- **Factory selling to a merchant exporter in India:** does not need one. The merchant's IEC goes on the shipping bill.
- **Service exporters:** need an IEC only if they want to claim Foreign Trade Policy benefits.
- **Exempt:** a few categories, such as goods for personal use and certain government and notified bodies.
## Documents to keep ready

DGFT now checks many details online against other government and bank records, so some uploads may not be asked for. Keep the scans ready anyway. DGFT can also verify the address physically after the IEC is issued.
- PAN of the business (the IEC is issued against it).
- Address proof of the business premises in the firm's name: electricity bill, rent agreement or sale deed.
- A bank account in the firm's name: cancelled cheque or bank certificate.
- Mobile number and email you will keep for years; DGFT sends all OTPs and notices there.
- A Class 3 digital signature (DSC), or an Aadhaar-linked mobile for Aadhaar e-sign.
- For companies, LLPs and partnerships: details of directors or partners.
## Step by step: apply on the DGFT portal

- Go to dgft.gov.in and register as an importer/exporter with your mobile number and email (OTP on both).
- Log in and open the IEC application (form ANF-2A) under the IEC services menu.
- Fill in the business name exactly as on PAN, the address, bank account, directors or partners, and any branch offices.
- Upload the documents the portal asks for.
- Pay the ₹500 fee online.
- Sign the application with your DSC or Aadhaar e-sign and submit.
- Download the IEC certificate from the portal and save the login. You will need it every year.
## Cost and how long it takes

The government fee is ₹500, paid once. There is no renewal fee, and the annual update is free if you do it between 1 April and 30 June. An agent may charge for filing, but the DGFT fee stays ₹500.
When PAN, bank and address details pass DGFT's online checks, the IEC is usually issued soon after you submit. If something does not match, the application goes to the regional DGFT office and takes longer. Most delays come from a name or address that differs between PAN, GST and the bank.
## The annual update: April to June, every year

Under the Foreign Trade Policy 2023, every IEC holder must update or confirm its IEC details online each year between April and June, even if nothing has changed. A no-change confirmation takes a few minutes and costs nothing.
Miss the window and the IEC can be deactivated. A deactivated IEC stops shipping bills at customs and holds up bank remittances. You can still file the update later (DGFT's fee schedule lists ₹200 for an update after the window), and the IEC is reactivated once it is done. Separately, DGFT's rules require you to update the IEC online within 30 days whenever your address, bank account, partners, directors or constitution change.
## Common mistakes

Next steps: register with your [export promotion council](http://localhost:8040/guide/rcmc-export-promotion-council), fix your [HS code](http://localhost:8040/guide/hs-code-for-export) and file a [GST LUT](http://localhost:8040/guide/gst-on-exports-lut-refund). The [export readiness check](http://localhost:8040/tools/export-readiness) shows what is still missing, and the full sequence is in [how to export from India](http://localhost:8040/guide/how-to-export-from-india).
Exportwalla's desk can do this paperwork with you, shipment by shipment, and you review and sign every filing; see [pricing](http://localhost:8040/pricing) or [talk to us](http://localhost:8040/contact).
- Business name on the IEC differs from PAN or GST registration.
- Bank account in the owner's personal name for a company or LLP.
- Factory address on GST but office address on IEC, with no branch added.
- Letting an agent keep the login and DSC. Keep your own credentials.
- Forgetting the April–June update, then finding the IEC deactivated during a shipment.
- Stopping at the IEC. Next you need the AD code registered at the port, a GST LUT and usually an RCMC.

**Try it on your own product:** [upload an invoice or photo](http://localhost:8040/app) to get your HS code, best countries, duty, buyers and a quote. Free.

**Get your IEC, RCMC and LUT done with us**We prepare the filings; your digital signature signs.Ask the desk

## Questions

**Is the IEC number the same as my PAN?**

Yes. Since July 2017 DGFT has used the PAN of the business as its IEC, and only one IEC can exist against one PAN. A proprietor's IEC is the owner's PAN; a company or LLP uses its own PAN. If you open a new company, it needs its own IEC.
**Does an IEC expire?**

No. It has no expiry date and no renewal fee. But you must update or confirm it online every year between April and June. If you skip this, DGFT can deactivate the IEC until you complete the update.
**Can I apply without a digital signature?**

Yes. The DGFT portal accepts Aadhaar-based e-sign as well as a Class 3 digital signature. For e-sign, the Aadhaar of the person signing must be linked to a mobile number that receives the OTP.
**I only sell to an exporter in India. Do I need an IEC?**

No. If the merchant exporter buys from you in India and exports in its own name, its IEC goes on the shipping bill. You need your own IEC only when you export in your own name, which also lets you claim incentives and refunds directly.
**My IEC was deactivated. What now?**

Log in to the DGFT portal and complete the pending annual update. DGFT's fee schedule lists ₹200 for an update filed after the April–June window. Once it is submitted, the IEC is reactivated and customs and banks can use it again.

## Official sources

- [DGFT: IEC profile management](https://www.dgft.gov.in/CP/?opt=iec-profile-management)
- [DGFT Public Notice 02/2025-26: Appendix 2K fees (IEC ₹500; annual update nil in April–June, ₹200 after)](https://content.dgft.gov.in/Website/dgftprod/35248419-7538-4a1f-9569-421dddabb26b/PN%2002-2025-26_0001%20Eng.pdf)
- [DGFT: Foreign Trade Policy 2023, chapter 2 (para 2.05, IEC)](https://content.dgft.gov.in/Website/dgftprod/4f665d2f-20cc-4887-ae6a-5ec912bc0d44/FTP2023_Chapter02.pdf)
- [DGFT: Handbook of Procedures, chapter 2 (IEC application and modification)](https://content.dgft.gov.in/Website/HBP_07_2026_Chapter_02.pdf)
- [DGFT notifications and public notices](https://www.dgft.gov.in/CP/?opt=notification)

# RCMC: register with the right export promotion council

**In short:** An RCMC (Registration-cum-Membership Certificate) shows you are a registered member of the export promotion council or commodity board for your product, such as CLE for leather, AEPC for garments or APEDA for rice. Apply on DGFT's e-RCMC service using your IEC. It is normally valid for five years and is needed for most Foreign Trade Policy benefits and for joining council fairs and buyer meets.

Apply on: **DGFT e-RCMC (common digital platform)**
Validity: **5 years, 1 April to 31 March**
APEDA fee: **₹5,000 + 18% GST**
Needed first: **IEC**

## What an RCMC is and why you need it

Each product family in India has an export promotion council (EPC) or commodity board. The list is in Appendix 2T of the Foreign Trade Policy. When you join the council for your main product, it issues an RCMC. DGFT and other agencies treat that certificate as proof that you are a registered exporter of that product.
- **Foreign Trade Policy benefits:** authorisations and benefits such as Advance Authorisation and EPCG ask for an RCMC.
- **Fairs and buyer meets:** councils run India pavilions, buyer-seller meets and delegations, often with government Market Access Support (MAS) under the Export Promotion Mission, which replaced the old Market Access Initiative (MAI).
- **Buyer enquiries and market data:** councils pass on enquiries and circulars to members.
- **Compulsory for some products:** APEDA products, spices (Spices Board) and marine products (MPEDA) need registration before you export at all.
## Which council for which product

Register with the council for the product that makes most of your exports; your town does not decide it, and the clusters above are only examples. You can hold more than one RCMC if you export in different product families.

| Your product | Council or board | Typical clusters |
| Leather footwear, bags, gloves, finished leather | Council for Leather Exports (CLE) | Kanpur, Agra, Chennai, Ambur |
| Garments, knitted or woven | Apparel Export Promotion Council (AEPC) | Tiruppur, Ludhiana, Noida |
| Cotton yarn, fabric, bed linen, towels | Cotton Textiles EPC (TEXPROCIL) | Panipat, Karur, Solapur |
| Handloom made-ups and furnishings | Handloom EPC (HEPC) | Panipat, Karur |
| Handicrafts, art metalware, wooden and decor items | EPC for Handicrafts (EPCH) | Moradabad, Jodhpur, Saharanpur |
| Carpets and floor coverings | Carpet EPC (CEPC) | Bhadohi, Panipat |
| Spices: cumin, fennel, chilli, turmeric | Spices Board (CRES) | Unjha, Guntur, Kochi |
| Rice, processed food, fruit, vegetables, meat | APEDA | Punjab, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh |
| Shrimp, fish and other marine products | MPEDA | Andhra coast, Kerala, Gujarat |
| Engineering goods, auto parts, machinery | EEPC India | Ludhiana, Rajkot, Pune |
| Many unrelated products, or none of the above | FIEO | All India |
## How to apply on DGFT e-RCMC

Renewals and amendments go through the same e-RCMC service. Most delays come from missing manufacturing proof or a name and address that do not match the IEC.
- Get your [IEC](http://localhost:8040/guide/how-to-get-iec-code) first. The RCMC is issued against it.
- Log in to the DGFT portal with your IEC-linked account and open e-RCMC, then apply for a new RCMC.
- Choose the registering authority (council or board), your products and whether you are a manufacturer or merchant exporter.
- Fill in the details and upload what the council asks for: GST registration, manufacturing proof such as Udyam, factory licence or FSSAI, and bank details.
- Pay the council's fee online. Each council sets its own fee and some also charge an annual membership subscription.
- Sign with DSC or Aadhaar e-sign and submit. The council reviews it and issues an e-RCMC that you download from the portal.
## Validity and keeping it alive

An RCMC is normally valid for five years. The period counts from 1 April of the licensing year in which it was issued and ends on 31 March five years later, unless the council specifies otherwise. Renew it online before it lapses, especially before you apply for an authorisation or book a council fair.
Councils may ask members for annual export returns and the yearly subscription. If your name, address, ownership or constitution changes, tell the council within one month, and update the RCMC when your products or exporter status change.
## APEDA, Spices Board and MPEDA: registration is compulsory

- **APEDA:** exporters of APEDA-listed products (rice, processed food, fresh produce, meat, dairy, honey and more) must register. APEDA issues its RCMC through the DGFT portal; the fee is ₹5,000 plus 18% GST (₹5,900) and validity is five years. Rice exporters also deal with APEDA's contract registration; see the [rice guide](http://localhost:8040/guide/how-to-export-rice-from-india).
- **Spices Board:** you cannot export spices without a CRES (Certificate of Registration as Exporter of Spices). It is issued for a three-year block, the fee differs for merchant and manufacturer exporters, and renewals are filed through the DGFT portal. See the [spices guide](http://localhost:8040/guide/how-to-export-spices-from-india).
- **MPEDA:** exporters of marine products must register with MPEDA. Processing plants that ship to the EU and several other markets also need approval through the Export Inspection Council. See the [shrimp guide](http://localhost:8040/guide/how-to-export-shrimp-from-india).
## Common mistakes

Product-wise steps are in the guides for [leather footwear](http://localhost:8040/guide/how-to-export-leather-footwear-from-india), [garments](http://localhost:8040/guide/how-to-export-garments-from-india) and [brass and handicrafts](http://localhost:8040/guide/how-to-export-brass-and-handicrafts-from-india). Check what else you need with the [export readiness check](http://localhost:8040/tools/export-readiness).
Exportwalla's desk can do this paperwork with you, shipment by shipment, and you review and sign every filing; see [pricing](http://localhost:8040/pricing) or [talk to us](http://localhost:8040/contact).
- Joining a general body when your product has a specific council or board.
- Letting the RCMC lapse just before applying for Advance Authorisation or booking a council fair.
- Exporting spices or APEDA products on the strength of an IEC alone.
- Name, address or exporter type on the RCMC that differs from the IEC.

**Try it on your own product:** [upload an invoice or photo](http://localhost:8040/app) to get your HS code, best countries, duty, buyers and a quote. Free.

**Not sure which council is yours?**Tell us your product and we register you with the right one.Ask the desk

## Questions

**Is RCMC compulsory for every exporter?**

Not for every product. You can export most goods with only an IEC. But you need an RCMC to claim most Foreign Trade Policy benefits, and registration with APEDA, the Spices Board or MPEDA is compulsory before exporting their products.
**How long is an RCMC valid?**

Normally five years, counted from 1 April of the year it was issued to 31 March five years later, unless the council says otherwise. Renew it online on the DGFT e-RCMC service before it expires.
**Which council should a Moradabad brass exporter join?**

Brass artware, decorative metal items and other handicrafts come under the Export Promotion Council for Handicrafts (EPCH). Industrial brass parts and fittings are engineering goods and come under EEPC India.
**What does an RCMC cost?**

Each council sets its own registration fee and some add an annual subscription. APEDA, for example, charges ₹5,000 plus 18% GST for an RCMC valid five years. Check the fee on your council's page in the DGFT e-RCMC service before paying.
**Can I hold RCMCs from two councils?**

Yes. If you export products from different families, for example garments and home textiles, you can register with each council. Use the RCMC that matches the product for which you claim a benefit.

## Official sources

- [DGFT: e-RCMC service](https://www.dgft.gov.in/CP/index.jsp?opt=e-rcmc)

- [APEDA: e-RCMC procedure circular](https://apeda.gov.in/sites/default/files/announcements/circular_Procedure_on__e_Rcmc.pdf)

# HS code for export: find the right code before you quote

**In short:** The HS code is the 6-digit product code every customs office in the world uses. India adds two digits (8-digit ITC-HS) on the shipping bill, and the buyer's country adds its own (UK and US use 10). Classify by reading the heading text and chapter notes under the General Rules of Interpretation. The code decides import duty, FTA eligibility and India's export incentive rates.

Global code: **6 digits (WCO Harmonized System)**
India: **8-digit ITC-HS on the shipping bill**
UK binding ruling: **ATaR, generally valid 3 years**
EU binding ruling: **BTI, valid 3 years**

## Three layers of the same code

The first six digits should be the same on your invoice, your shipping bill and the buyer's import entry. The digits after six are national and will differ. If the first six differ, one side has classified wrongly, and that is when customs asks questions.

| Level | Digits | Who sets it | What it decides |
| Harmonized System (HS) | 6 | World Customs Organization; used by more than 200 countries | The common base. FTA rules of origin are written on it. |
| India: ITC-HS / Customs Tariff | 8 | CBIC tariff and DGFT's ITC(HS) | Shipping bill line, export policy (free or restricted), drawback and RoDTEP rates |
| Buyer's country | 8 to 10 or more | Importing country's customs | Import duty, quotas, licences and product rules. UK and US use 10 digits, EU uses 8 (CN) and 10 (TARIC). |
## How to classify, in plain words

Classification follows six General Rules of Interpretation (GRIs) that every country applies the same way. In practice:
- Describe the product precisely: what it is made of, how it is made, what it does and how it is sold (single item, set, part).
- Find the likely chapter, then read the four-digit heading text and the section and chapter notes. These are the law; chapter titles are only a guide (GRI 1).
- An unfinished or unassembled article that already has the character of the finished one goes where the finished one goes (GRI 2).
- If two headings fit, the more specific description wins. For mixtures and sets, the material or part that gives the essential character decides. If still tied, take the heading that comes last in number order (GRI 3).
- If nothing fits, use the heading for the most similar goods (GRI 4). Normal packing and cases go with the goods (GRI 5).
- Apply the same logic inside the heading to reach six digits, then pick India's eight-digit line (GRI 6).
- Cross-check with India's tariff, the buyer's tariff and published rulings abroad.
## Two examples

Try your own product in the [HS code finder](http://localhost:8040/tools/hs-code-finder), or upload an invoice to the [free workspace](http://localhost:8040/app) and it suggests the code with duty and markets.
- **Moradabad brass statue for the home:** a decorative ornament of base metal goes to heading 8306 (statuettes and other ornaments), not to chapter 74 for copper and brass articles. The section notes keep chapter 83 articles out of chapter 74, so reading the notes settles it. (An original sculpture made by an artist is different: chapter 97.)
- **Kanpur leather handbag with cotton lining:** heading 4202, and the subheading follows the outer surface material, here leather. The lining does not change it.
## Why the code matters so much

- **Duty abroad:** the buyer's duty is set per tariff line. See it with the [import duty tool](http://localhost:8040/tools/import-duty).
- **FTA benefit:** a trade deal cuts duty only for lines in its schedule, and each line has its own rule of origin. See [trade agreements](http://localhost:8040/fta) and the [certificate of origin guide](http://localhost:8040/guide/certificate-of-origin).
- **Indian export policy:** DGFT's ITC(HS) shows whether an item is free, restricted or prohibited for export.
- **Incentives:** RoDTEP and drawback rates are listed per tariff line; see [RoDTEP and drawback](http://localhost:8040/guide/rodtep-and-duty-drawback).
- **GST:** the GST rate on your inputs and supplies is also linked to the code.
## Binding rulings: lock the code before a big order

If the duty difference between two codes is large, get a binding ruling instead of arguing after the goods land.
**UK (ATaR):** an Advance Tariff Ruling from HMRC is legally binding on the commodity code and is generally valid for three years. The applicant needs a GB EORI number, so in practice your UK importer applies. HMRC replies in 30 to 120 days.
**EU (BTI):** a Binding Tariff Information decision is binding in every EU country for three years. The EU importer applies through the EU Customs Trader Portal with an EORI number; there is no fee for the decision itself.
**India:** the Customs Authority for Advance Rulings (benches in Delhi and Mumbai) can rule on the classification of goods before they are imported or exported. It is worth it when a restriction or a large incentive depends on the line.
## Mistakes that cost money

Exportwalla's desk can do this paperwork with you, shipment by shipment, and you review and sign every filing; see [pricing](http://localhost:8040/pricing) or [talk to us](http://localhost:8040/contact).
- Putting the buyer's 10-digit code on the Indian shipping bill instead of the Indian 8-digit line.
- Copying a competitor's or supplier's code without reading the heading notes.
- Choosing a line because its RoDTEP or drawback rate is higher. Misclassification leads to recovery with interest and penalties.
- Vague invoice descriptions like 'handicraft items' or 'garments'. Write material, construction and use.
- One code for a mixed set when the parts are sold separately.

**Try it on your own product:** [upload an invoice or photo](http://localhost:8040/app) to get your HS code, best countries, duty, buyers and a quote. Free.

**Get your HS code confirmed**Send us your product. We confirm the 8-digit code before you quote.Ask the desk

## Questions

**Is the HS code the same in every country?**

Only the first six digits. Every country that uses the Harmonized System shares the 6-digit code, then adds its own digits. India uses 8 digits, the UK and US use 10, and the EU uses 8 for its Combined Nomenclature and 10 for TARIC.
**Which code goes on the Indian shipping bill?**

The 8-digit Indian tariff item (ITC-HS). The buyer's 10-digit code belongs on their import declaration, though you can also show it on the invoice to help them. The first six digits of both should match.
**Who decides the correct code?**

The customs authority of each country, using the General Rules of Interpretation. Your declaration is your responsibility in India; the importer is responsible abroad. A binding ruling removes the doubt.
**Can my buyer get a binding ruling in the UK or EU?**

Yes. A UK importer with a GB EORI applies to HMRC for an Advance Tariff Ruling, generally valid three years. An EU importer applies for Binding Tariff Information, valid three years across the EU. Send them full product details and photos.
**What happens if I use the wrong code?**

Customs can reassess duty, recover incentives such as RoDTEP or drawback with interest, and levy penalties. Abroad, the buyer may lose the FTA rate and pay the full duty, which usually lands back on you as a claim.

## Official sources

- [WCO: what is the Harmonized System](https://www.wcoomd.org/en/topics/nomenclature/overview/what-is-the-harmonized-system.aspx)
- [GOV.UK: apply for an Advance Tariff Ruling](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/apply-for-an-advance-tariff-ruling)
- [GOV.UK: what you need for a binding commodity code decision](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/check-what-youll-need-to-get-a-legally-binding-decision-on-a-commodity-code)
- [European Commission: validity of BTI decisions](https://taxation-customs.ec.europa.eu/validity-period-bti-decisions_en)
- [European Commission: European Binding Tariff Information](https://taxation-customs.ec.europa.eu/online-services/online-services-and-databases-customs/european-binding-tariff-information-ebti_en)
- [WCO: HS 2022 Section XV notes (Note 2: chapter 82 and 83 articles excluded from chapter 74)](https://www.wcoomd.org/-/media/wco/public/global/pdf/topics/nomenclature/instruments-and-tools/hs-nomenclature-2022/2022/1500_2022e.pdf)
- [WCO: HS 2022 chapter 83 (heading 83.06)](https://www.wcoomd.org/-/media/wco/public/global/pdf/topics/nomenclature/instruments-and-tools/hs-nomenclature-2022/2022/1583_2022e.pdf)

# Certificate of origin: which one you need and how to get it

**In short:** A certificate of origin proves where goods were made. A preferential certificate lets your buyer pay the lower FTA duty; apply for it on DGFT's Trade Connect eCoO platform (trade.gov.in), issued by EIC, MPEDA, the Textiles Committee or another listed agency. A non-preferential certificate from a chamber or council only proves Indian origin. Some deals, such as India–UK CETA, also accept the exporter's own origin declaration.

Platform: **Trade Connect eCoO (trade.gov.in)**
Preferential CoO fee (DGFT schedule): **₹600**
India–UK CETA proof valid: **12 months**
Keep origin records: **5 years under India–UK CETA**

## Preferential, non-preferential and self-declared

A non-preferential certificate never gets the buyer a lower duty. If the buyer wants the FTA rate, they need the preferential proof named in that agreement. Check your deal on the [trade agreements](http://localhost:8040/fta) page.

| Type | What it does | Who issues it |
| Preferential certificate | Buyer pays the lower duty under a trade agreement | Agencies listed for each agreement in DGFT Appendix 2B: EIC for all goods, MPEDA for marine products, Textiles Committee for textiles and made-ups, and others |
| Non-preferential certificate | Proves Indian origin only; asked for under letters of credit and by some importing countries | Chambers of commerce and councils listed in DGFT Appendix 2E |
| Origin declaration or statement | Exporter declares origin, where the agreement allows | You, the exporter; for example India–UK CETA, or the EU GSP statement on origin by a REX-registered exporter |
## Rules of origin in plain words

A preferential certificate is only valid if the product meets that agreement's rule of origin for its HS line. There are three common tests:
- **Wholly obtained:** grown, mined, fished, or born and raised in India. Indian rice, cumin from Unjha and shrimp farmed in Andhra pass easily.
- **Change of tariff classification:** imported materials must change heading (CTH, 4 digits), subheading (CTSH, 6 digits) or chapter. Imported finished leather (chapter 41) made into shoes (chapter 64) changes chapter.
- **Value content:** a minimum share of the product's value must come from the partner countries. The percentage and the method are set line by line in each agreement.
- **Never enough on their own:** simple operations such as packing, labelling, sorting or mixing.
- **Tolerance:** a small share of non-originating material can be ignored. Under India–UK CETA it is 12.5% of value for industrial goods (chapters 25 to 98), and 7.5% or 12.5% by value or weight for farm and food chapters.
## Apply on Trade Connect (eCoO)

Non-preferential certificates must be filed electronically on trade.gov.in since 1 January 2025, and preferential certificates are issued on the same eCoO platform. DGFT lists ₹600 for issuing a preferential certificate and ₹200 for each non-preferential certificate.
- Log in to trade.gov.in with your IEC-linked DGFT account. Keep your DSC or Aadhaar e-sign active in the profile.
- Open Certificate of Origin and choose preferential or non-preferential, then the agreement and destination country.
- Select the issuing agency: EIC, MPEDA or the Textiles Committee for preferential; a chamber or council for non-preferential.
- Enter invoice details, the HS code and the origin criterion (wholly obtained, change of heading or value content), and upload the invoice plus cost sheet or input invoices where a value test applies.
- Pay the agency fee online and submit. The agency may ask questions or inspect the goods.
- Download the digitally signed eCoO with its QR code and send it to the buyer with the invoice before the goods arrive.
## Self-declaration where the deal allows it

**India–UK CETA (in force from 15 July 2026):** a UK importer can claim the lower duty with an origin declaration by the exporter or producer, a certificate from an issuing authority, or the importer's own knowledge backed by documents. The declaration follows the agreement's template, is in English, travels with the invoice and is valid for 12 months. On Trade Connect you can generate a self-declared eCoO for the UK without a fee, using a DSC linked to your IEC, or choose an agency instead. The UK can also waive proof for consignments up to £1,000 customs value. See [India–UK CETA](http://localhost:8040/fta/india-uk-ceta) and [exporting to the UK](http://localhost:8040/export-to/united-kingdom).
**EU GSP:** India has lost GSP for many industrial product groups for 2026–2028, but it still applies to others. Where it applies, the proof is a statement on origin on the invoice by an exporter registered in the REX system; consignments of originating goods up to €6,000 can carry a statement from any exporter. The [India–EU FTA](http://localhost:8040/fta/india-eu-fta) is a separate deal.
Most of India's other agreements, such as [India–UAE CEPA](http://localhost:8040/fta/india-uae-cepa) and [India–Australia ECTA](http://localhost:8040/fta/india-australia-ecta), work with agency-issued certificates. Check the deal page before you ship.
## Record keeping and verification

The importing country can verify origin months after the goods are cleared. Keep the bill of materials, input invoices, cost sheet, production records and supplier declarations for every shipment where you claimed origin. India–UK CETA requires exporters to keep them for five years. If you cannot prove origin, the buyer pays full duty and penalties, and you usually lose the customer.
## Common mistakes

Check your line and the rule first with the [HS code guide](http://localhost:8040/guide/hs-code-for-export) and the [import duty tool](http://localhost:8040/tools/import-duty).
Exportwalla's desk can do this paperwork with you, shipment by shipment, and you review and sign every filing; see [pricing](http://localhost:8040/pricing) or [talk to us](http://localhost:8040/contact).
- Sending a non-preferential certificate when the buyer needs the preferential one.
- HS code or invoice number on the certificate that differs from the invoice and shipping bill.
- Claiming 'change of heading' without checking the product-specific rule for that line.
- A trader declaring origin without the manufacturer's cost data to back it.
- Claiming a deal for a line that is not in its tariff schedule.

**Try it on your own product:** [upload an invoice or photo](http://localhost:8040/app) to get your HS code, best countries, duty, buyers and a quote. Free.

**File your certificate of origin with us**We check the rule of origin and prepare the certificate with you.Ask the desk

## Questions

**What is the difference between preferential and non-preferential certificates?**

A preferential certificate is issued under a trade agreement and lets the buyer pay the lower agreement duty, if the goods meet its rules of origin. A non-preferential certificate only proves the goods are Indian and gives no duty cut.
**Where do I apply for a certificate of origin in India?**

On DGFT's Trade Connect platform, trade.gov.in, using your IEC-linked login. You choose the agreement and the issuing agency, fill in invoice and origin details, pay the fee and download a digitally signed eCoO.
**Can I self-certify origin for UK exports?**

Yes. Under India–UK CETA, the UK accepts an origin declaration completed by the exporter or producer. You can generate a self-declared eCoO on Trade Connect without a fee, with a DSC linked to your IEC. Keep the proof of origin for five years.
**How long is a certificate of origin valid?**

It depends on the agreement. Under India–UK CETA, a certificate or origin declaration is valid for 12 months from issue or completion. Check the deal page for other agreements.
**Which agency issues preferential certificates?**

DGFT Appendix 2B lists agencies per agreement. The Export Inspection Council covers all goods, MPEDA covers marine products, and the Textiles Committee covers textiles and made-ups under most agreements.

## Official sources

- [DGFT Trade Connect (eCoO)](https://trade.gov.in/)
- [GOV.UK: UK–India CETA chapter 3, rules of origin](https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/687e58acae8555bab409a070/uk_india_ceta_chapter_3_rules_of_origin.pdf)

# GST on exports: LUT, IGST refund and ITC refund

**In short:** Exports are zero-rated under GST. Either file a Letter of Undertaking (form GST RFD-11) for the financial year and export without paying IGST, then claim refund of unused input tax credit in form RFD-01; or pay IGST on the export invoice and get it back automatically, because the shipping bill itself counts as the refund claim. Most stuck refunds come from invoice mismatches between the shipping bill and GSTR-1, or a missing EGM.

LUT form: **GST RFD-11, once per financial year**
Goods must leave India: **Within 3 months of invoice (LUT)**
ITC refund form: **GST RFD-01**
IGST refund claim: **Shipping bill, processed via ICEGATE**

## Two ways to export under GST

Pick one route per invoice and keep it consistent across the invoice, the shipping bill and GSTR-1. Mixing them is a common reason for blocked refunds.

|  | Route 1: export under LUT | Route 2: pay IGST, claim refund |
| At the time of export | No IGST on the invoice; it states supply under LUT without payment of IGST | Charge IGST on the export invoice and pay it in GSTR-3B (credit can be used) |
| What you get back | Unused input tax credit | The IGST you paid |
| How you claim | RFD-01 on the GST portal | No separate form: the shipping bill is the claim |
| Suits | Most MSME exporters | Exporters with a large credit balance who want automatic refunds |
## File the LUT (form GST RFD-11)

Any registered person can use an LUT, except one prosecuted for tax evasion above ₹250 lakh, who must give a bond with a bank guarantee instead. A 2017 CBIC circular treats the LUT as accepted if the officer does not act within three working days. Under the LUT, goods must leave India within three months of the invoice date. If they do not, you pay the IGST with interest within 15 days, and the LUT facility is withdrawn until you do.
- Log in to gst.gov.in and go to Services, User Services, Furnish Letter of Undertaking (LUT).
- Select the financial year. The LUT covers that year and expires on 31 March, so file a new one each April before the first export.
- Tick the declarations, give two witnesses' names and addresses, and sign with DSC or EVC.
- Note the ARN. Quote the LUT reference on every export invoice under it.
## IGST route: the shipping bill is your refund claim

Under Rule 96 of the CGST Rules, the shipping bill is treated as the refund application once these conditions are met:
- GSTN sends your Table 6A data to ICEGATE.
- Customs matches it with the shipping bill and EGM.
- If everything matches, a refund scroll is generated and the money goes to your registered bank account.
- Check the status on ICEGATE; error codes tell you what failed.
- The shipping line or airline has filed the export manifest (EGM) covering your shipping bill.
- You have filed a valid GSTR-3B for the month, paying at least the IGST shown on the exports.
- GSTR-1 Table 6A lists each export invoice with the same number, date and value as on the shipping bill.
- You have completed Aadhaar authentication on the GST portal.
- Your bank account is registered with customs at the port, so the refund has somewhere to land.
## LUT route: refund of unused credit in RFD-01

- On the GST portal, file RFD-01 for refund of accumulated input tax credit on exports without payment of tax. You can cover one or several tax periods.
- Upload the statement of export invoices with shipping bill numbers, dates and EGM details.
- Work out the eligible amount: zero-rated turnover × net input tax credit ÷ adjusted total turnover. Credit on capital goods is left out of net ITC.
- File within two years of the relevant date. For goods sent by sea or air, that is the date the ship or aircraft leaves India.
- The officer can sanction 90% as a provisional refund within seven days of acknowledgement for zero-rated supplies, with the final order due within 60 days of a complete application.
## Why export refunds get stuck

- **Invoice mismatch (ICEGATE code SB005):** the invoice number in GSTR-1 differs from the one on the shipping bill. If GSTR-1 is wrong, amend it through Table 9A. If the shipping bill is wrong, take it up with customs at the port.
- **EGM not filed or faulty (SB002; SB006 for ICD gateway EGM):** ask the shipping line or your forwarder to file or correct it.
- **GSTR-3B short:** IGST claimed in Table 6A is more than the IGST paid in GSTR-3B for that month.
- **Bank account not validated:** the account registered with customs fails validation, so the scroll cannot be paid.
- **Wrong route:** IGST charged on the invoice but the shipping bill filed under LUT, or the other way round.
- **Aadhaar authentication pending** on the GST portal.
## Where e-BRC and FIRC come in

When the buyer's payment arrives, your bank sends the remittance details to DGFT, and you self-certify and generate the e-BRC against that remittance on DGFT's e-BRC system (the bank may also give you a FIRA or FIRC). For goods, the refund itself rests on the shipping bill and EGM. But if payment is not received within the period RBI allows, the GST refund has to be paid back with interest. Service exporters need the bank realisation proof to claim at all. Reconcile e-BRCs with shipping bills every month.
Related: [payment terms](http://localhost:8040/guide/letter-of-credit-and-payment-terms), [customs clearance](http://localhost:8040/guide/export-shipping-and-customs-clearance) and [RoDTEP and drawback](http://localhost:8040/guide/rodtep-and-duty-drawback). To work out your export price, use the [export price calculator](http://localhost:8040/tools/export-price-calculator).
Exportwalla's desk can do this paperwork with you, shipment by shipment, and you review and sign every filing; see [pricing](http://localhost:8040/pricing) or [talk to us](http://localhost:8040/contact).

**Try it on your own product:** [upload an invoice or photo](http://localhost:8040/app) to get your HS code, best countries, duty, buyers and a quote. Free.

**Stuck IGST refund or LUT question?**We find what is blocking it and fix it with your CA.Ask the desk

## Questions

**Is GST charged on exports from India?**

Exports are zero-rated. You either export under an LUT without paying IGST and claim refund of unused input credit, or pay IGST and get it refunded. Either way the tax does not stay in the export price.
**How often do I file the LUT?**

Once per financial year, on the GST portal in form RFD-11. It expires on 31 March, so file a fresh LUT in April before your first export invoice of the new year.
**Do I need to file RFD-01 for an IGST refund on goods?**

No. For goods exported on payment of IGST, the shipping bill is treated as the refund application once the EGM and a valid GSTR-3B are filed. RFD-01 is for refund of unused credit under an LUT, among other cases.
**My IGST refund shows SB005. What does it mean?**

SB005 means the invoice number on the shipping bill does not match the one in GSTR-1 Table 6A. Correct GSTR-1 through Table 9A if the return is wrong; if the shipping bill is wrong, approach the customs officer at the port of export.
**What is the time limit for an ITC refund claim on exports?**

Two years from the relevant date. For goods exported by sea or air, that is the date the ship or aircraft carrying them leaves India.

- [CBIC: CGST Rule 96 (IGST refund on exports)](https://taxinformation.cbic.gov.in/content/html/tax_repository/gst/rules/cgst_rules/active/chapter10/rule96_v1.00.html)

# RoDTEP and duty drawback: what they pay and how to claim

**In short:** RoDTEP refunds taxes built into your export price that no other scheme refunds, such as VAT on fuel, mandi tax and electricity duty, as a transferable duty credit e-scrip. All Industry Rate drawback refunds customs duty on inputs, in cash. You claim both through the shipping bill on ICEGATE. Rates differ by tariff line in DGFT Appendix 4R/4RE and CBIC's drawback schedule. RoDTEP is currently notified up to 31 December 2026.

RoDTEP notified until: **31 December 2026**
RoDTEP rates: **DGFT Appendix 4R (DTA) and 4RE (AA, SEZ, EOU)**
Drawback rates: **CBIC All Industry Rate schedule**
Claim on: **Shipping bill, ICEGATE**

## What each scheme pays back

The two schemes cover different taxes, so a normal shipment can get both. What you must not do is claim a line or category that the conditions exclude.

|  | RoDTEP | All Industry Rate drawback |
| Refunds | Central, state and local taxes in the export product that are not refunded elsewhere | Customs duty paid on inputs used in the export product |
| Paid as | Duty credit e-scrip in your ICEGATE ledger; transferable | Cash to your bank account registered with customs |
| Rate set by | DGFT, Appendix 4R and 4RE, % of FOB, often with a per-unit cap | CBIC drawback schedule, % of FOB, with caps on many lines |
| How you claim | Declare it in the shipping bill, then generate the e-scrip on ICEGATE | Declare the drawback serial number in the shipping bill |
## Where to find the rate for your product

Rates are set per 8-digit tariff line and change, so do not copy a rate from a blog or an old quote. Check the official schedule for your exact line before you price the order.
- **RoDTEP:** the RoDTEP page on dgft.gov.in has Appendix 4R (exports from the Domestic Tariff Area) and Appendix 4RE (exports by Advance Authorisation holders, SEZ units and EOUs). Tariff items were realigned with the Customs Tariff from 1 May 2026.
- **Drawback:** CBIC notifies the All Industry Rate schedule and amends it from time to time. Use the schedule in force on your shipping bill date.
- **Brand rate:** if no All Industry Rate exists for your product, or it is far below the duty you actually paid, you can apply to the jurisdictional Commissioner for a brand rate with your cost data.
- Not sure of your line? Start with the [HS code guide](http://localhost:8040/guide/hs-code-for-export) and the [HS code finder](http://localhost:8040/tools/hs-code-finder).
## Where RoDTEP stands in November 2026

DGFT Notification 41/2026-27 of 30 September 2026 continues RoDTEP up to 31 December 2026 for exports from DTA units, Advance Authorisation holders, SEZ units and EOUs, at the rates and value caps in force on 30 September 2026. Other conditions are unchanged.
The government has extended the scheme in short steps: to 31 March 2026, then 30 September 2026, then 31 December 2026. Nothing has been notified yet for shipments after 31 December 2026. Rates can also change at short notice: in February 2026 DGFT cut all rates and caps to half (Notification 60/2025-26), then restored them a month later with retrospective effect (Notification 66/2025-26). Check the DGFT RoDTEP page before you build RoDTEP into a quote for 2027 shipments.
## How to claim on ICEGATE

- Register on ICEGATE with your IEC and DSC. Register your AD code and bank account at each port you ship from.
- In the shipping bill, your customs broker enters the 8-digit tariff item, the drawback serial number and the RoDTEP claim for each item, with the declarations the schemes require.
- After let export order and the EGM, drawback is processed and paid to your registered bank account.
- For RoDTEP, a scroll is generated after the EGM. Create your RoDTEP credit ledger on ICEGATE and generate the e-scrip, signed with your DSC.
- Use the e-scrip to pay basic customs duty on your own imports, or transfer it on ICEGATE to an importer who buys it. The whole balance of a scrip transfers at once.
- Watch the expiry date shown in the ledger and use or sell the scrip before it lapses.
## Payment realisation and common mistakes

Both benefits assume the buyer pays. If export proceeds are not realised within the period RBI allows, the amounts can be recovered. Keep e-BRCs matched to shipping bills; see [GST refunds and e-BRC](http://localhost:8040/guide/gst-on-exports-lut-refund).
- Leaving out the RoDTEP declaration in the shipping bill; adding it later is difficult.
- Wrong tariff line, or a line picked for its higher rate. Customs recovers the excess with interest and penalties.
- Bank account not registered or validated with customs, so drawback cannot be paid.
- EGM errors that hold up both the drawback and the RoDTEP scroll.
- Forgetting the per-unit cap. The benefit is the lower of rate × FOB and the cap.
- Inflated FOB values. They invite verification and recovery.
## Build it into your price, carefully

RoDTEP and drawback can be a few percent of FOB, which matters on thin margins. Put the official rate for your line into the [export price calculator](http://localhost:8040/tools/export-price-calculator), and treat RoDTEP for shipments after 31 December 2026 as uncertain until the government notifies an extension. Related: [customs clearance](http://localhost:8040/guide/export-shipping-and-customs-clearance) and [FOB and CIF pricing](http://localhost:8040/guide/export-pricing-fob-cif).
Exportwalla's desk can do this paperwork with you, shipment by shipment, and you review and sign every filing; see [pricing](http://localhost:8040/pricing) or [talk to us](http://localhost:8040/contact).

**Try it on your own product:** [upload an invoice or photo](http://localhost:8040/app) to get your HS code, best countries, duty, buyers and a quote. Free.

**Claim RoDTEP and drawback correctly**We check your shipping bills so nothing is missed.Ask the desk

## Questions

**Can I claim RoDTEP and drawback on the same shipment?**

Yes, as a rule. Drawback refunds customs duty on inputs, while RoDTEP refunds other embedded taxes that are not refunded under any other scheme. Both are claimed in the same shipping bill, subject to each scheme's conditions.
**Is RoDTEP available in 2027?**

As of November 2026, RoDTEP is notified only up to 31 December 2026 (DGFT Notification 41/2026-27). Whether it continues after that depends on a new notification. Check the RoDTEP page on dgft.gov.in before quoting for 2027 shipments.
**Where do I find the RoDTEP rate for my product?**

In DGFT's Appendix 4R for exports from the Domestic Tariff Area, or Appendix 4RE for Advance Authorisation, SEZ and EOU exports, on the RoDTEP page of dgft.gov.in. Look up your exact 8-digit tariff item and any per-unit cap.
**How is drawback paid?**

All Industry Rate drawback is paid in cash to the bank account you registered with customs at the port, after the let export order and the EGM. The shipping bill itself is the claim, so no separate application is needed.
**What can I do with a RoDTEP e-scrip?**

Use it to pay basic customs duty on your own imports, or transfer it on ICEGATE to another importer, usually at a small discount. A scrip transfers in full, and it lapses after its expiry date.

## Official sources

- [DGFT: RoDTEP rates and notifications](https://www.dgft.gov.in/CP/?opt=RoDTEP)
- [DGFT Notification 41/2026-27: RoDTEP continued to 31 December 2026](https://content.dgft.gov.in/Website/dgftprod/be0b7ef2-e1e3-48a1-adc8-529ba4de48c5/RODTEP%20NOTIFICATION.pdf)
- [DGFT Notification 66/2025-26: restoration of RoDTEP rates](https://content.dgft.gov.in/Website/dgftprod/575d3fa4-c6a0-4aeb-9eb1-386ff7e3c22b/Notification%2066%20English_0001-merged.pdf)
